description: Policy for the benchmark gates. References live beside the benchmarks in conformance/bare-runtime/baseline-*.json, conformance/link-benchmark/measured.json, and conformance/miniapp-benchmark/measured-desktop.json; this file holds only the thresholds and the rule about changing a reference.

endToEnd.description: Thresholds for the end-to-end latency and throughput benchmarks (link handshake setup, mini-app spawn/kill and watchdog rate). Ratios are normalised so that larger is always worse, whichever direction the metric runs, so one pair of thresholds covers both polarities.
endToEnd.rationale: Wider than the crypto thresholds in both directions, and for the opposite reason. These measurements involve process spawn, a loopback socket, and a Docker peer, so their variance on a shared runner is much larger than a tight crypto loop's — a 1.4x warn band would be noise if it failed, which is why it only warns. The 2x failure cliff is what the two runners already used before they were gates (link setup p95 at 2x, mini-app spawn at 3x); 2x is the tighter of the two and neither benchmark exceeds it today. The point of this gate is not to catch a 20% drift on a noisy host — it is that a 3x latency regression in message delivery currently passes every gate in the repository.
endToEnd.unrecordedReferences: A zero or absent reference fails rather than passes. conformance/link-benchmark/measured.json shipped as all zeros with a comparison written `if (baseline.setupP95Ms > 0)`, so the benchmark measured, printed, and asserted nothing for over a month. 'No baseline' and 'passing' must not be the same state.

rationale: The failure threshold stays at 0.5 because throughput is machine-dependent: the references were recorded on the ci-reference host, and a healthy developer laptop lands ~0.8x on x25519 while being entirely fine. Tightening the failure threshold without per-host references would produce a gate that fails for the machine it ran on rather than for the change under test. The warn band exists so that drift between 0.8x and the cliff is visible on the published page while it is still small, instead of surfacing only on the day a 50% regression lands.
changingAReference: Raising a reference is ordinary: measure on the reference host and edit the baseline file. Lowering one fails the gate against the base branch, because a reference that can be lowered silently is not a reference — `record-benchmark.mjs` with no --compare overwrites it with whatever the current machine measured, which is exactly the hole this guard closes. A genuine lowering (slower algorithm accepted for another reason) needs the reason in the commit message.
